TypedRisks.name: Unlicensed curators making unilateral risk decisions
TypedRisks.description: Curator TVL grew from 300 million USD to 7 billion USD, a 2,200 percent increase, with the top five curators holding roughly 43 percent share and no major curator licensed. Depositors delegate credit decisions to entities with no regulatory obligation and no capital at risk.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Role separation into Owner, Curator, Allocator and Sentinel, timelocks, abdication, gates, adapter registry and fee caps of 50 percent performance and 5 percent management
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Curator AUM concentration, and the delay between a new market listing and its first published risk rationale
TypedRisks.sourceLabel: Chorus One on DeFi curators in 2025

TypedRisks.name: Hardcoded oracle prices blocking liquidation
TypedRisks.description: Stream Finance vault oracles hardcoded xUSD near one dollar, so when the token collapsed liquidations could not trigger and utilisation hit 100 percent. Bad debt ran into the hundreds of millions across at least fifteen Morpho vaults plus Euler.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Post-incident scrutiny of hardcoded and rate-based oracles, and market close-only settings
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Any market where the oracle is a fixed constant or an internal exchange rate rather than a market-derived price

TypedRisks.name: Donation-based inflation attack with a faulty oracle
TypedRisks.description: Morpho's own documentation warns that on Vaults V1 an attacker can donate into a market with a mispriced oracle and inflict losses on the vault, and that supply caps do not protect against this. A market sitting in the withdrawal queue with a cap of zero is still vulnerable and the loss is unbounded by the cap.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Documented warning, adapter registry, and guidance to remove markets entirely rather than only zeroing caps
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Any vault holding a market with a non-market oracle, and unexpected share balance increases in a vault it did not initiate

TypedRisks.name: LP-token oracle manipulation via flash loan
TypedRisks.description: The Aerodrome sAMM-cUSDO/USDC LP oracle read raw pool reserves combined with a Chainlink USDC feed, a cUSDO ERC-4626 rate and a hardcoded one dollar USDO price. An attacker flash-loaned 6,666,666.67 USDC, inflated the LP value, borrowed 363,935 USDC and self-liquidated.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Market set to close-only with allocations zeroed, and the curator fully compensated the 49,303.14 USDC of bad debt
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Any oracle that reads spot AMM reserves, and any collateral whose price includes a hardcoded stablecoin leg

TypedRisks.name: Last-depositor bank run in Vaults V1.1
TypedRisks.description: Morpho documents that in Vault V1.1 the last depositor to exit bears the bad debt left in the vault. This creates a rational incentive to withdraw first at the earliest sign of trouble.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Documented explicitly, plus Sentinel role and timelocks to slow adverse changes
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Withdrawal velocity relative to vault liquidity, and any vault where realised bad debt is not yet socialised

TypedRisks.name: Adapter removal frontrunning
TypedRisks.description: Removing an adapter without first setting its caps to zero can be frontrun, letting an attacker act between the two operations. This is an operational sequencing hazard rather than a code defect.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Documented requirement to zero caps before calling removeAdapter
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Any removeAdapter transaction not preceded by a cap-zeroing transaction in the same block sequence

TypedRisks.name: Reverting oracle putting a market into a degraded state
TypedRisks.description: If an oracle reverts, borrow and liquidate calls revert with it, leaving a market that cannot be de-risked. Positions become frozen at whatever health factor they held at the moment of failure.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Documented degraded-state behaviour so curators can plan a fallback
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Oracle call revert rate per market, and time since the last successful price update

TypedRisks.name: Curator and venue concentration
TypedRisks.description: The top three curators, Steakhouse, Sentora and Gauntlet, together managed about 5.14 billion USD, and Morpho was the largest single venue at 2.91 billion USD. A single curator's error propagates across a large share of the deposit base.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Vault-level isolation and per-vault caps, plus public curator dashboards
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Share of protocol TVL controlled by the top three curators, and overlap of the same collateral across their vaults

TypedRisks.name: Withdrawal queuing and rate spikes during stress
TypedRisks.description: During the Stream Finance fallout withdrawals were queued and rates spiked as high as 190 percent, with 80 percent of withdrawals completing within three days. Even Steakhouse and Gauntlet USDC vaults that had no xUSD exposure became briefly illiquid.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Interest rate curves that price scarcity, and withdrawal queues that avoid a disorderly first-mover race
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Vault utilisation at or near 100 percent, and the length of the withdrawal queue in hours
TypedRisks.sourceLabel: Chorus One on DeFi curators in 2025

TypedRisks.name: Curator discretion used against borrowers
TypedRisks.description: In the PT-USD0++ / USDC vault, users complained that curators cut the supply allocation to 20 million USD and drove rates to three figures for up to 30 hours, which they characterised as punitive. The curator justified it by an imbalanced Pendle SY/PT pool that limited liquidation capacity.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Public forum disclosure of curator rationale, and Morpho's documented role and timelock framework
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Sudden allocation cuts and borrow rate jumps in a vault with no corresponding collateral price move
TypedRisks.sourceLabel: Morpho forum thread on PT-USD0++ vault curators

TypedRisks.name: Public Allocator enabling cross-vault contagion
TypedRisks.description: After the Resolv exploit, 6.2 million USD of bad debt reached Morpho vaults via the Public Allocator, with Gauntlet accounting for 96 percent of the total losses. Morpho's supply() accepts an onBehalf parameter, so anyone can credit market shares to a vault without its authorisation.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Curators setting supply caps to zero on affected markets, and a compensation plan announced
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Inbound supply() calls naming a vault as onBehalf that the vault did not initiate
TypedRisks.sourceLabel: Oak Research on the Resolv USR hack

TypedRisks.name: Over-reliance on third-party risk endorsements
TypedRisks.description: Steakhouse Financial published a report five days before the Resolv hack calling the protocol institutionally rigorous and crisis-ready, and other curators used it to justify exposure. Steakhouse itself had no direct USR exposure while the curators relying on its work took the losses.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Public post-incident scrutiny and calls for higher due diligence, real-time monitoring and built-in circuit breakers
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Whether a curator's allocation rationale rests on its own analysis or on another party's published report
TypedRisks.sourceLabel: Oak Research on the Resolv USR hack

TypedRisks.name: Immutable core with no parameter correction path
TypedRisks.description: Morpho's core is immutable and the LLTV of a market cannot be changed once created. A market created with an unsafe LLTV or oracle can only be abandoned, never fixed.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Immutability audited by Certora formal verification, with a Cantina bug bounty of 2,500,000 USD
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Number of live markets flagged as unsafe that remain listed because they cannot be reparameterised

TypedRisks.name: Front-end and SDK misconfiguration routing approvals
TypedRisks.description: On 10 April 2025 a front-end and SDK misconfiguration sent token approvals to the Bundler3 contract instead of the intended adapters. One user's bundled transaction was intercepted, though by a whitehat MEV bot rather than an attacker.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Rollback within four minutes, contracts themselves unaffected, public incident write-up
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Approval targets in front-end transactions diverging from the canonical adapter address list

TypedRisks.name: Vault shares used as collateral
TypedRisks.description: Morpho documentation states that Vault V1.0 is not recommended for use as collateral. Recursive use of vault shares stacks oracle, bad debt and liquidity risk from the underlying markets into a single collateral token.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Explicit documentation warning, and the V1.1 revision
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Any market listing a V1.0 vault share as collateral, and the underlying market composition of that vault

TypedRisks.name: Structural leverage inside collateral issuers
TypedRisks.description: Stream Finance reached a peak TVL of 520 million USD on 160 million USD of deposits, implying 3.25 times structural leverage, before disclosing a 93 million USD external manager loss on 4 November 2025. Morpho markets accepted the resulting token as collateral without visibility into that leverage.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Post-incident emphasis on issuer transparency, and market close-only settings after the fact
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Issuer TVL divided by verifiable external deposits, and any refusal or delay in publishing reserve attestations

CATEGORY#Entity|PROTOCOL#morpho.TradFiAnalogue: a securitisation platform plus the fund managers who buy its tranches. Morpho Blue is the standardised, immutable issuance rail; MetaMorpho and Vaults V2 curators are the asset managers making the actual credit selection on behalf of end investors.

bull.claim: Scale has compounded fast: Morpho Blue holds $7.516B TVL with $4.077B borrowed across 40-plus chains as of 26 July 2026, second only to Aave in this set (DefiLlama).

The capital and investor base is the strongest in the sector: $175M in June 2026 co-led by Paradigm, a16z crypto and Ribbit, with Apollo Funds, Circle Ventures and VanEck participating at roughly a $2B valuation (Lex Substack).

Enterprise distribution is proven: Morpho was the first protocol integrated directly by a major enterprise, with Coinbase issuing over $300M in bitcoin-backed loans through it, alongside Trust Wallet, Binance Wallet, Safe and Ledger (Morpho blog).

Immutability removes governance risk from live markets: parameters persist in perpetuity, market creation needs no vote, and governance's only economic lever is a fee switch capped at 25% of borrower interest (Morpho docs, Morpho docs).

bear.claim: Isolation does not prevent losses, it only localises them: the November 2025 Stream Finance collapse left roughly 3.6% bad debt in the MEV Capital vault and mapped roughly $285M of potential exposure across DeFi (Binance Square, The Block).
The credit event repeated within nine months: a Resolv exploit hit Morpho vaults in July 2026 and MORPHO fell 4.6% (CoinMarketCap).

Depositors are exposed to curator quality with no protocol backstop, which Morpho's own documentation acknowledges by publishing curator security considerations and a bad-debt handling tutorial (Morpho docs, Morpho docs).
Third-party risk scoring is mid-grade, not top-tier: Hindenrank assigned Morpho a B- grade at $7.1B TVL in its 2 May 2026 report (Hindenrank).

AssetCoverage.assetStrategy: Morpho has no protocol level asset list at all. Anyone can deploy an immutable market defined by a collateral token, a loan token, an LLTV and an oracle, so "supported assets" means whichever markets curators and vaults have actually funded. There are no supply or borrow caps at the market level; exposure limits live in the ERC-4626 vaults that allocate into markets. Liquidation incentive is derived from LLTV rather than set per asset, and [the Morpho liquidation documentation](https://docs.morpho.org/build/borrow/concepts/liquidation/) states that at an LLTV of 86 percent the liquidation incentive factor is approximately 1.05, a 5 percent bonus, with the protocol taking no fee; Morpho does not publish the general formula on that page, so bonuses at other LLTVs are marked n.a. below. The practical consequence is that Morpho's Ethereum book is dominated by a handful of LLTV tiers (86, 91.5, 94.5, 96.5 percent) and by long tail collateral that no shared pool would list: tokenised credit tranches, Pendle principal tokens, RWA style yield tokens and curator specific dollars. CATEGORY#Entity|PROTOCOL#morpho.RiskPosture: Morpho has almost no protocol-level risk and almost all of its risk in the layer above it. The immutable core is formally verified by Certora with a 2.5 million USD Cantina bounty ([Morpho docs](https://docs.morpho.org/learn/resources/risks/)), and in three documented loss events the core behaved exactly as specified. The damage came from curators: who they listed, what oracles they accepted and how fast they reacted. Every major loss traces to a collateral issuer failing while an oracle told the market nothing was wrong, in the Aerodrome LP case ([ClearstarLabs](https://forum.morpho.org/t/post-mortem-aerodrome-cusdo-usdc-amm-lp-oracle-manipulation-on-morpho-lending-market/1794)), in Stream's hardcoded xUSD price ([TokenIntel](https://tokenintel.org/reports/stream-finance-post-mortem-2026-05-21.html)) and in Resolv's hardcoded USR oracle exploited through the Public Allocator ([Oak Research](https://oakresearch.io/en/analyses/investigations/the-resolv-usr-hack-curators-face-their-responsibilities)). Morpho's own documentation is unusually candid about the residual hazards, including donation attacks that supply caps do not stop and the last-depositor bank run in Vaults V1.1 ([Morpho security considerations](https://docs.morpho.org/curate/concepts/security-considerations/)). The structural problem is that curator TVL grew 2,200 percent to 7 billion USD with no licensing and heavy concentration in five firms ([Chorus One](https://chorus.one/reports-research/defi-curators-in-2025-navigating-chaos-building-resilience)). Net posture: low technological risk in the base layer, critical and recurring counterparty and governance risk in the curated layer, with loss magnitude driven almost entirely by curator judgement.

Under the interim Proof of Authority model the Neptune Mutual Association could pause the protocol and reverse incident-reporting decisions via emergency resolutions, concentrating significant discretionary power. OpenZeppelin also flagged that the protocol has a large number of very privileged roles requiring careful key management.

A complex 44-contract codebase with intricate storage and access-control patterns. Audits (OpenZeppelin, BlockSec, Hacken) found high-severity issues that were subsequently addressed, but residual smart-contract risk remains inherent.

Cover pools are funded with stablecoin liquidity; the protocol's ability to pay claims depends on pooled reserves. OpenZeppelin flagged risk of insufficient liquidity when computing policy coverage commitments, and a stablecoin depeg would impair reserve value.

Cover Creators are approved at the team's discretion and covers reference third-party protocols and exchanges; the value of a policy depends on the correct scoping of the covered counterparty and event.

OrgStructure.description: The protocol was built and operated by a small, largely pseudonymous team publishing under the 'Neutra Finance' identity on Medium and X. No verified individual founder identities are publicly documented; the team collaborated with GMX, RoboLabs, and CertiK on the V2 vault.

Risks.description: The vaults are complex automated contracts (GLP handling, perp position management, rebalancing). Despite SolidProof and CertiK audits, audited contracts can still contain exploitable bugs, and the protocol now appears unmaintained, increasing the risk of undiscovered or unpatched vulnerabilities.

The protocol appears abandoned/dormant: no public activity after early 2024, negligible NEU trading volume, and the primary website domains no longer resolve. Depositors risk stranded funds, unmaintained hedges, and inability to reach the team.

The strategy is entirely dependent on GMX (GLP as the yield source and GMX perps as the hedge venue). Any GMX exploit, GLP pool imbalance, insolvency, or downtime directly threatens both legs of the position; Neutra has no control over GMX.

Both GLP pricing and GMX perpetual liquidations rely on GMX's oracle price feeds. Oracle manipulation, staleness, or divergence can misprice the hedge, trigger premature liquidation of the short leg, or break delta neutrality.

GLP is heavily weighted to stablecoins; a depeg of a constituent stablecoin (or of the deposit asset DAI) would impair the long leg's value independently of the BTC/ETH hedge, causing losses the delta-neutral design does not offset.

The protocol runs solely on Arbitrum. Arbitrum sequencer downtime or congestion could block timely rebalancing/withdrawals, leaving the leveraged short hedge unmanaged during volatile periods and exposing positions to liquidation.

OrgStructure.description: A UK-registered discretionary mutual that wraps the DAO. It has a Board with deliberately limited powers; members can replace Board members at any time. Founded by Hugh Karp, who launched the protocol on Ethereum mainnet in 2019.
OrgStructure.name: Nexus Mutual Ltd (UK legal wrapper)

Risks.description: The mutual can only pay claims up to what the Capital Pool holds. A cluster of large correlated losses, or a sharp fall in the value of pool assets (ETH/stETH), can push capital below the Minimum Capital Requirement, forcing the mutual to stop selling cover and impairing its ability to honor outstanding cover.

Cover payouts are discretionary and decided by NXM-staked members via claims assessment. Voter apathy, whale concentration, or a member majority acting in self-interest could wrongly reject valid claims (leaving policyholders unpaid) or approve invalid ones (draining the pool).

The Capital Pool, RAMM, staking-pool and cover contracts hold and move all member capital on-chain. A bug or exploit in this stack could drain reserves directly, the same failure mode the mutual exists to insure against, making it its own single point of failure.

V2 delegates underwriting to permissionless staking-pool managers who choose which products to back and how to price them. Mispriced or over-concentrated pools can leave the mutual under-reserved for a given risk, and delegators bear burn risk from a manager's poor underwriting.

Nexus Mutual operates as an unregulated UK discretionary mutual, not a licensed insurer, and NXM membership is KYC-gated with native NXM non-transferable. Regulatory reclassification of its cover as insurance, or of NXM/wNXM as a security, could restrict operations or market access.

TradFiComparison.differences: Cover is discretionary (payouts voted by members under cover wording, not a legally binding insurance contract), it is unregulated as insurance, capital is on-chain crypto, and underwriting/claims are executed by smart contracts and token-holder governance.
TradFiComparison.similarity: Like a traditional mutual insurer, the members are the owners: they pool capital, share risk, keep any underwriting surplus, and collectively decide on claims rather than paying a shareholder-owned carrier.

TradFiComparison.differences: Anyone can spin up a staking pool permissionlessly, capital is NXM staked on-chain, and there is no regulated managing-agent structure or legally binding policy.
TradFiComparison.similarity: V2 staking pools resemble Lloyd's syndicates: specialist underwriters bring capital, pick which risks to back, and price them, while passive capital providers can back the underwriters.

Components.description: Notional's core product. fCash is an ERC-1155 token representing a claim to a fixed amount of an underlying asset at a specific future maturity. Lenders buy positive fCash at a discount and redeem it 1:1 at maturity for a fixed return; borrowers mint negative fCash to receive cash today and repay a fixed amount later. fCash trades against Prime Cash in maturity-specific AMM liquidity pools where the ratio of Prime Cash to fCash sets the fixed interest rate. This is how Notional delivers fixed-rate, fixed-term lending and borrowing on-chain.
Components.name: fCash fixed-rate markets

Components.description: Introduced in V3, the prime money market lets users lend and borrow at variable rates, integrating with the fixed-rate markets. Deposits are represented as Prime Cash. Fixed-rate debt automatically converts to variable-rate debt at maturity with no settlement penalty, and variable positions serve as the underlying liquidity that fixed-rate pools trade against.
Components.name: Prime money market (variable-rate lending)

Components.description: Whitelisted external smart contracts that execute pre-approved yield strategies (e.g. Curve, Balancer, Uniswap LP or staking strategies) funded by fixed- or variable-rate borrowing from Notional. A user deposits collateral, borrows against it, and the combined capital is deployed into the vault; vault assets are recognized as collateral against the debt, enabling leveraged (up to ~10x on some strategies) exposure while paying interest only on the borrowed portion. Positions are overcollateralized and subject to liquidation.
Components.name: Leveraged vaults

Components.description: NOTE is the ERC-20 governance token of the Notional protocol. Holders propose, vote on, and implement changes to system parameters and smart contracts (one vote per NOTE) via Notional Improvement Proposals through on-chain governance. NOTE is also used to incentivize liquidity providers and, historically, could be staked (sNOTE) to backstop the protocol.
Components.name: NOTE governance token

Faq.question: Is Notional V3 still operating?
Faq.answer: No, not as a going concern. On 19 June 2025 the team said V3 would keep running but that it would "gradually withdraw support" and zero out NOTE liquidity incentives by the end of 2025 ([Introducing Notional Exponent](https://blog.notional.finance/introducing-notional-exponent/)). In November 2025 V3 was announced to cease operations on mainnet and Arbitrum, with cross-asset lending positions auto-migrated to Aave ([KuCoin news wire](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/notional-v3-to-cease-operations-on-mainnet-and-arbitrum-users-to-be-migrated-to-aave)). DefiLlama shows only $3.58m of residual TVL as of 26 July 2026 ([DefiLlama Notional](https://defillama.com/protocol/notional)).

Faq.question: What caused the losses at the end?
Faq.answer: A Balancer vulnerability. Notional V3 carried bad debt of 641.4 ETH on mainnet plus 80.2 ETH on Arbitrum, and holders of the Balancer and Aura leveraged vaults lost 100 percent of their positions ([KuCoin news wire](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/notional-v3-to-cease-operations-on-mainnet-and-arbitrum-users-to-be-migrated-to-aave)). One report puts the total loss at over 721 ETH ([AInvest](https://www.ainvest.com/news/notional-v3-protocol-suffers-721-eth-loss-due-balancer-vulnerability-2511/)).

Faq.question: What is Notional Exponent and is it the same product?
Faq.answer: No. Exponent is "a leveraged yield protocol that enables users to maximize returns on DeFi yield strategies with leverage", built on top of external lending markets such as Morpho to source borrow liquidity for looping ([Notional Exponent docs](https://docs.notional.finance/exponent)). It is a leveraged yield vault business, not fixed-rate term lending, so the fixed income primitive itself did not survive the transition.

Faq.question: How large is Exponent today?
Faq.answer: Small. DefiLlama shows $483,689 of TVL on Ethereum for Notional Exponent as of 26 July 2026, against peers such as Yield Basis at $121.71m and Homora V2 at $110.27m ([DefiLlama Notional Exponent](https://defillama.com/protocol/notional-exponent)).

Faq.question: How did fCash actually price a fixed rate?
Faq.answer: As a discount note. Lending 100 USDC for six months at 5 percent mints fCash of 100 × e^(0.05×0.5) = 102.53, so the rate is embedded in the exchange rate between cash and fCash ([Notional docs, using fCash](https://docs.notional.finance/notional-v3/fcash/using-fcash)). Borrowers minted an offsetting positive and negative fCash pair against collateral.

Faq.question: Does NOTE still govern anything?
Faq.answer: NOTE remains the governance token, voted through the "Notional Snapshot" by holders on Mainnet and Arbitrum, with a quorum currently set at 1,000,000 NOTE and a simple majority pass rule ([Notional docs, Snapshot voting](https://docs.notional.finance/notional-governance/notional-governance-process/notional-governance/snapshot-voting)). NOTE was also used for the 100,000 NOTE incentive programme at the Exponent launch ([Notional Exponent launch details](https://blog.notional.finance/notional-exponent-launch-details/)).

Faq.question: Is there another protocol called Exponent?
Faq.answer: Yes, and they are unrelated. The Solana protocol Exponent Finance is a separate company and should not be confused with Notional Exponent, which is documented at docs.notional.finance/exponent ([Notional Exponent docs](https://docs.notional.finance/exponent)).

Incidents.title: Exploit
Incidents.description: The Balancer V2 hack, detected by Notional at 2:52 AM ET, drained the Balancer pools underpinning five Notional leveraged vaults: rETH/WETH, wstETH/WETH and rsETH/WETH on Arbitrum, and ezETH/WETH and rsETH/WETH on mainnet.
Incidents.amountUsdDisplay: n.a. (632.8 ETH mainnet plus 80.2 ETH Arbitrum of bad debt)
Incidents.outcome: Vault holders lost 100% of their positions. Protocol reserves of roughly 100 thousand USD on mainnet and 18 thousand USD on Arbitrum were written to zero, plus about 205 thousand USD and 161,450 USD of non ETH reserves converted to ETH. ETH lenders were then haircut 56.019% on mainnet and 19.244% on Arbitrum.

Incidents.title: Wind-down
Incidents.description: Following the Balancer losses Notional closed remaining vault positions, migrated cross currency borrowers to Aave using individually deployed Gnosis Safes, and made full distributions.
Incidents.outcome: Notional V3 was wound down on both Ethereum mainnet and Arbitrum. Notional Exponent later launched as the successor protocol on 26 January 2026.

CATEGORY#Entity|PROTOCOL#notional.LongDescription: Notional built fixed-rate, fixed-term lending and borrowing on Ethereum using fCash, a token representing a fixed amount of an asset at a fixed future date. A lender swaps cash for fCash at a rate set by the pool: 100 USDC lent for six months at 5 percent yields fCash of 100 × e^(0.05×0.5) = 102.53, and a borrower mints an offsetting positive and negative fCash pair against collateral ([Notional docs, using fCash](https://docs.notional.finance/notional-v3/fcash/using-fcash)). V3 removed the hard cliff at maturity by auto-converting matured fixed-rate debt into variable-rate debt, which allowed penalty-free rolls ([Introducing Notional V3](https://blog.notional.finance/introducing-notional-v3/)). This entity is not in steady state. Notional V3 is winding down: the team announced on 19 June 2025 that it would gradually withdraw support, and in November 2025 V3 was announced to cease operations on mainnet and Arbitrum following bad debt from a Balancer vulnerability ([Introducing Notional Exponent](https://blog.notional.finance/introducing-notional-exponent/), [KuCoin news wire](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/notional-v3-to-cease-operations-on-mainnet-and-arbitrum-users-to-be-migrated-to-aave)). The successor product, Notional Exponent, a leveraged yield vault protocol built on Morpho borrow liquidity, went live on 26 January 2026 ([Notional Exponent launch details](https://blog.notional.finance/notional-exponent-launch-details/), [Notional Exponent docs](https://docs.notional.finance/exponent)).

Risks.description: All borrowing and leveraged-vault positions are overcollateralized in volatile crypto assets (ETH, wstETH, cbETH, wBTC, ARB, etc.). A sharp drop in collateral value can push a position below its required collateralization ratio and trigger liquidation, causing loss to the borrower.

Notional relies on complex custom contracts (fCash ERC-1155 accounting, maturity-specific AMM pools, external leveraged vaults). Despite 17+ audits, bugs in these contracts or in the whitelisted vault strategy code could lead to loss of funds.

Collateral valuation and liquidation for borrowers and leveraged vaults depend on price oracles. Manipulated, stale, or inaccurate oracle prices could cause faulty liquidations or allow undercollateralized borrowing.

Leveraged vaults deploy borrowed capital into external protocols (e.g. Curve, Balancer, Uniswap, liquid-staking tokens). A failure, exploit, or depeg in one of those external strategy protocols would directly impair vault positions and the loans backing them.

Protocol parameters, collateral listings, vault whitelisting and contract upgrades are controlled by NOTE-token governance. Concentrated NOTE holdings or a malicious/erroneous proposal could change risk parameters or upgrade contracts in ways that harm users.

TypedRisks.name: Contagion from an integrated external protocol
TypedRisks.description: Notional's leveraged vaults deposited user capital into third party pools, so a vulnerability outside Notional could destroy vault equity. This materialised on 3 November 2025 when the Balancer V2 hack wiped out five Notional vaults.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Post incident the affected vaults were closed and Notional V3 was wound down. Notional Exponent runs real time monitoring and exploit prevention with Hypernative.
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Exploit alerts on any protocol a live vault deposits into, sudden change in vault share price

TypedRisks.name: Bad debt socialised onto lenders as a haircut
TypedRisks.description: When vault collateral is destroyed, the resulting bad debt is not absorbed by an insurance fund but passed to the lenders of the borrowed currency. In November 2025 ETH lenders took a 56.019% haircut on mainnet and 19.244% on Arbitrum.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Reserves are burned first, then the haircut is applied pro rata. Reserves proved far too small relative to the loss.
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Reserve balance as a percentage of outstanding vault debt in each currency
linkedAssetsUnmatched: ETH lending markets on Ethereum mainnet

TypedRisks.name: Reserve buffer far too small to absorb a tail loss
TypedRisks.description: Notional's protocol reserves were written to zero in the incident, roughly 100 thousand USD on mainnet and 18 thousand USD on Arbitrum, plus about 205 thousand USD and 161,450 USD of non ETH reserves converted to ETH. Against 632.8 ETH of mainnet bad debt and 80.2 ETH on Arbitrum, the buffer covered a small fraction of the loss.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Reserves fully applied before haircuts, remediation plan closing positions and migrating borrowers
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Ratio of reserve balances to total vault debt, growth rate of reserves versus growth of leveraged exposure

TypedRisks.name: Total loss of leveraged vault equity
TypedRisks.description: Leveraged vault holders sit in the first loss position and can be wiped out entirely. In the Balancer incident vault holders lost 100% of their positions.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Supply caps per vault, minimum borrow sizes, requirement that positions remain liquidatable, audits of each vault strategy
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Vault share price, vault utilisation against its cap

TypedRisks.name: Vault economic insolvency independent of exploit
TypedRisks.description: Notional documentation identifies economic risk where a vault strategy loses value faster than it can be liquidated, leaving the position insolvent. This is distinct from smart contract failure and arises from the strategy itself.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Supply caps, minimum borrow sizes, liquidatability requirement, per vault leverage limits
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Vault health factor distribution, time between liquidation trigger and execution
linkedPartnersUnmatched: External strategy protocols integrated by each vault

TypedRisks.name: Liquidation failure producing bad debt for nToken holders
TypedRisks.description: nToken holders are exposed to bad debt if the protocol fails to liquidate an undercollateralised account in time. The nToken absorbs the shortfall.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Collateral haircuts, debt buffers, liquidation incentives, oracle price deviation limits
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Number of accounts below the liquidation threshold that remain unliquidated, gas conditions during volatility

TypedRisks.name: nToken redemption risk under high utilisation
TypedRisks.description: nToken holders may be unable to redeem at fair value when lending market utilisation is high, because the underlying liquidity is committed to fCash. Exit then requires selling into a thin market or waiting.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Utilisation dependent interest rate curves, published redemption mechanics
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Lending market utilisation rate, nToken secondary market discount to NAV

TypedRisks.name: Interest rate risk on fCash positions
TypedRisks.description: fCash is a fixed rate claim whose present value moves inversely with market interest rates. A holder exiting before maturity can realise a loss even with no credit event.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Fixed maturities so the position pulls to par if held, oracle rate TWAPs used for valuation
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Change in implied fixed rates across maturities, mark to market on open fCash

TypedRisks.name: Oracle deviation and TWAP valuation risk
TypedRisks.description: Collateral valuation relies on external price oracles with deviation limits, and fCash valuation relies on oracle rate TWAPs. A manipulated or stale feed distorts both liquidation triggers and portfolio value.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Oracle price deviation limits, TWAP smoothing of fCash rates, supply caps
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Oracle deviation limit breaches, TWAP versus spot divergence

TypedRisks.name: Smart contract risk in core protocol and vault strategies
TypedRisks.description: Notional documentation identifies smart contract risk in both the core protocol and in the external protocols that vault strategies integrate with. The Balancer Vault Strategy was among the audited components and still produced total vault loss through the upstream protocol.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Multiple audits including Sherlock in October 2022 for leveraged vaults and the Balancer Vault Strategy, Immunefi bug bounty
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: New audit findings, unaudited vault deployments

TypedRisks.name: Governance parameter risk
TypedRisks.description: Collateral haircuts, debt buffers, supply caps and oracle deviation limits are all set by NOTE and sNOTE governance through NRCs and NIPs voted on Snapshot. Mis-set parameters directly determine how much bad debt a shock produces.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Formal proposal process, published parameter tables
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Parameter change proposals on Snapshot, gap between proposed and prevailing market volatility

TypedRisks.name: Protocol discontinuity and forced migration
TypedRisks.description: Notional V3 was wound down on both Ethereum mainnet and Arbitrum after the Balancer incident rather than recapitalised. Users had to exit and cross currency borrowers were migrated to Aave through individually deployed Gnosis Safes.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Structured remediation plan with full distributions and assisted migration
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Governance signalling on protocol continuation, TVL trend after an incident

TypedRisks.name: Successor protocol is new and unproven
TypedRisks.description: Notional Exponent went live on 26 January 2026 with mAPOLLO and mHYPER vaults, a completely new codebase replacing the wound down V3. New leveraged yield code carries elevated risk in its first operating months regardless of audit coverage.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Full audits by Sherlock and MixBytes, 250 thousand USD Immunefi bug bounty, real time monitoring and exploit prevention with Hypernative
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Time since launch without incident, TVL growth rate versus audit and monitoring maturity

TypedRisks.name: Curator and external liquidity dependency in Exponent
TypedRisks.description: Exponent vault strategies are supplied by third party managers and lending liquidity comes from an external curator on Morpho. Notional itself states liquidity will be low at launch and depends on allocation decisions it does not control.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Named partners with track records, staged rollout across vaults
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Morpho vault allocation to Notional markets, borrow rate spikes from low liquidity

bull.claim: The successor product launched with institutional-grade process: two USDC vaults with named external strategists (Hyperithm and Apollo Crypto), audits by Sherlock and Mixbytes, a $250,000 Immunefi bounty and Hypernative monitoring (Notional Exponent launch details).
The team retains a long security record, including Sherlock audits completed 1 May 2023 and 1 June 2024 and a Code4rena review on 16 July 2022 (Immunefi Notional Exponent).

Exponent leverages Morpho rather than rebuilding a lending market, which lowers the capital needed to reach scale, and the first vault shipped with Clearstar as curator within three days of launch (Notional Exponent is Live).
The V3 wind-down was executed with user migration rather than abandonment, with cross-asset lending positions auto-migrated to Aave (KuCoin news wire).

bear.claim: **Current status: the original fixed income protocol is closing.** V3 was announced to cease operations on mainnet and Arbitrum in November 2025, and residual TVL is $3.58m as of 26 July 2026 versus a business that once offered tenors out to 20 years (KuCoin news wire, DefiLlama Notional, Messari report).
Users took real, uninsured losses: 641.4 ETH of bad debt on mainnet plus 80.2 ETH on Arbitrum, and 100 percent loss for Balancer and Aura leveraged vault holders (KuCoin news wire).
The successor is subscale at $483,689 of TVL as of 26 July 2026, orders of magnitude behind the leveraged yield peers DefiLlama lists alongside it (DefiLlama Notional Exponent).

The pivot abandons the fixed income category entirely. Exponent is described as a leveraged yield protocol built on Morpho borrow liquidity, not a fixed-rate term lending market (Notional Exponent docs).

AssetCoverage.assetStrategy: Notional's original design was a true fixed-term order book: lenders and borrowers trade fCash, a zero-coupon claim on a specific currency at a specific maturity, against Prime Cash on a set tenor ladder of 3 month, 6 month, 1 year, 2 year, 5 year, 10 year and 20 year points, with quarterly rolls and a per-currency `max market index` limiting how far out a currency trades ([Notional fCash maturities docs](https://docs.notional.finance/v3-risk-parameters/fcash-markets/fcash-maturities.md)). Risk is managed through a pairwise collateral framework rather than a single global LTV: each currency has a collateral haircut and a debt buffer, and the effective max LTV falls out of the specific collateral and debt pair ([Notional max LTV parameters sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Dm6dN5nXqJWhDAV3k313OT3bjqbwQ9qTJ2noq1xJRi0/edit?usp=sharing), linked from the [max LTV table docs page](https://docs.notional.finance/notional-v3/borrower-resources/max-ltv-table.md)). The critical thing to record for July 2026 is that this V3 system is being wound down: after the November 3, 2025 Balancer V2 hack impaired five leveraged vaults, Notional announced a full wind-down of V3 on Mainnet and Arbitrum ([Notional Balancer hack response](https://blog.notional.finance/balancer-hack-response/)). The forward strategy is Notional Exponent, a curated leveraged-vault product that launched January 26, 2026 with only two USDC vaults, mHYPER and mAPOLLO, both built on Midas Protocol tokenized strategies ([Exponent launch details](https://blog.notional.finance/notional-exponent-launch-details/), [Exponent is live](https://blog.notional.finance/notional-exponent-is-live/)).

CATEGORY#Entity|PROTOCOL#notional.RiskPosture: Notional's failure mode was composability, not its own code. Its lending and fCash machinery worked as designed, but its leveraged vaults had deposited user capital into Balancer V2, and when Balancer was exploited in November 2025 the loss travelled straight through: vault holders lost everything, the protocol's reserves proved to be a rounding error against the damage, and mainnet ETH lenders were haircut more than 56%. That is the important lesson, because it shows that in Notional's design the lenders, not an insurance fund, are the ultimate backstop. Rather than recapitalise, the team wound V3 down on both chains and migrated borrowers out to Aave. The successor, Notional Exponent, launched in January 2026 with Sherlock and MixBytes audits, a 250 thousand USD Immunefi bounty and Hypernative monitoring, but it is a new codebase with thin launch liquidity that again depends on external curators and strategy providers. Anyone underwriting Exponent is underwriting the same composability question with better monitoring and no track record yet.

Competitors.differences: Securitize operates as regulated infrastructure (transfer agent, broker-dealer, ATS) serving institutional issuers like BlackRock, Apollo, and KKR, with high minimums. Ondo is a consumer/DeFi-facing issuer that repackages such institutional funds into permissionless, lower-minimum, composable tokens (OUSG ~$5k, USDY retail) and also builds tokenized equities.

Faq.answer: Paladin is a DeFi ecosystem of governance protocols and markets that unlock the value of on-chain voting power. Its products let token holders lend, delegate, incentivize, or index governance power, turning votes into a yield-bearing 'money lego'. Core products include the Quest vote-incentive marketplace, the Warlord (WAR) governance index, hPAL liquid staking, and Paladin Lending.
Faq.question: What is Paladin?

Faq.answer: Quest calculates the value of a vote in advance, so an incentive provider fixes a cost-per-vote and total budget before the round. Rewards go to voters who fill the target objective (sorted oldest-to-newest), rewarding loyalty, and any unfilled budget is refundable pro-rata. Unlike Votium-style auctions where you can be outbid and lose your spend, Quest gives predictable pricing and returns unused budget.
Faq.question: How is Quest different from a bribe marketplace like Votium?

Faq.answer: WAR is a governance index token minted by depositing CVX and/or AURA. Warlord vote-locks the underlying and delegates it to earn vote incentives. Staking WAR (stkWAR) pays rewards in WETH, harvests BAL/CRV as auraBAL/cvxCRV, and auto-compounds earned AURA/CVX into more WAR. Users redeem WAR for the underlying, which is queued for each asset's unlock date.
Faq.question: What is the WAR token and how does Warlord work?

Faq.answer: PAL is Paladin's native governance token. hPAL (Holy PAL) is the staked/locked version used to govern Paladin DAO: staking PAL mints hPAL 1:1 and accrues PAL rewards, while locking hPAL for 3 months to 2 years boosts rewards (up to x6) and grants extra voting power. Staked hPAL requires a 10-day cooldown plus 2-day unstaking window to withdraw.
Faq.question: What are PAL and hPAL?

Faq.answer: Depositors put a governance token into a PalPool and receive a PalToken representing their share plus yield. A borrower opens a PalLoan, a clone contract that holds the borrowed tokens and delegates their voting power to the borrower for the loan duration, without ever transferring the underlying tokens to the borrower directly.
Faq.question: How does Paladin Lending let you borrow voting power?

Risks.description: Paladin runs multiple interacting contract systems (PalPools/PalLoans, Quest, Warlord/WAR, hPAL staking/locking). Code4rena contests found high- and medium-severity issues (e.g. 2 HIGH + 14 MEDIUM in the 2022 Holy PAL contest), so bugs in delegation, minting or reward accounting remain a core risk.

The protocol and products (e.g. Warlord asset inclusion, resource allocation via PGM proposals) are governed by hPAL voters. Concentration of hPAL or captured proposals could redirect delegated voting power or treasury resources against smaller holders' interests.

Warlord and the Autovoter delegate user voting power to a Paladin-controlled delegation address that manages CVX/AURA/vlLIQ locks and claims WETH incentives. Users rely on that operator to vote optimally and distribute rewards honestly; mismanagement or a compromised delegate address is a direct counterparty risk.

Paladin's revenue and product utility depend heavily on the external 'vote market' meta around Curve, Convex, Aura and Balancer. A collapse in gauge-vote demand, veTOKEN emissions, or the underlying DEXs would sharply reduce vote-incentive value flowing through Quest and Warlord.

WAR is backed by illiquid vote-locked CVX and AURA that unlock only on staggered schedules. Redeeming WAR queues withdrawals to each asset's unlock date, so holders face lock-up/exit-liquidity risk and potential discount to backing during stress.

Faq.answer: PancakeSwap is a decentralized exchange (DEX) launched in September 2020 on the BNB Smart Chain. It began as a lower-cost, faster alternative to Ethereum-based DEXs like Uniswap and has grown into a multi-product DeFi platform offering swaps, yield farming, an IFO launchpad, prediction markets, lotteries and NFTs. It is the dominant DEX on BNB Chain and now operates across multiple chains.
Faq.question: What is PancakeSwap?

Faq.answer: CAKE is PancakeSwap's native utility and governance token. It is used to earn and pay farming/staking rewards, participate in IFOs (via iCAKE limits), buy lottery tickets, and vote on governance proposals via Snapshot. CAKE has shifted to a deflationary model with weekly token burns and repeated emission reductions.
Faq.question: What is the CAKE token used for?

Faq.answer: PancakeSwap was built and is maintained by an anonymous team known as 'Chefs' working in the 'Kitchen,' reportedly more than a dozen members including two co-leads (pseudonyms 'Hops' and 'Thumper'). The protocol is open-source, community-governed via Snapshot, and received a strategic investment from Binance Labs in June 2022.
Faq.question: Who runs PancakeSwap?

Faq.answer: PancakeSwap Infinity is the protocol's modular AMM architecture that succeeds v3. It introduces programmable 'hooks' that execute custom logic around pool actions (swaps, liquidity changes, initialization, donations), enabling features like dynamic fees and custom oracles, alongside more gas-efficient pool types (CLAMM and LBAMM).
Faq.question: What is PancakeSwap Infinity?

Faq.answer: An Initial Farm Offering (IFO) is PancakeSwap's launchpad mechanism for new tokens. Using the 'Overflow' model, participants commit CAKE and receive a token allocation proportional to their share of total commitments, with unused funds returned at claim. A PancakeSwap profile is required and iCAKE sets the maximum commit limit for public sales.
Faq.question: What is an IFO on PancakeSwap?

Risks.description: CAKE tokenomics have been changed repeatedly through Snapshot governance — including the deflationary shift, successive emission cuts and the abrupt retirement of the veCAKE gauges model in Tokenomics 3.0 (Apr 2025). The veCAKE removal drew strong opposition from large stakeholders such as Cakepie DAO, who called it non-transparent and damaging to projects built on that model, illustrating governance and roadmap-change risk.

PancakeSwap originated on and remains heavily concentrated on BNB Chain, a network with a small, relatively centralized validator set closely associated with Binance. Concentration on BNB Chain exposes users to that chain's centralization, uptime and dependency risks even as PancakeSwap expands multi-chain.

The protocol is built and controlled by an anonymous team ('Chefs'), so there is no publicly identifiable, legally accountable operator. Anonymous leadership limits accountability and recourse if the team acts against user interests or disappears.

PancakeSwap comprises many interacting contracts (v2, v3 CLMM, Infinity hooks, cross-chain bridges, farms, lottery, prediction). Infinity's programmable hooks in particular expand the attack surface — CertiK has published security considerations specifically on Infinity hooks — and any exploit in these contracts could cause loss of pooled funds.

Liquidity providers on the AMM are exposed to impermanent loss and to the risk of holding volatile or low-quality tokens; because listing is permissionless, pools can contain scam or thinly-traded assets, exposing LPs and traders to depeg/rug and price-manipulation risk.

Faq.question: What exactly do I own when I buy a PT?
Faq.answer: A claim on one unit of the underlying yield bearing asset at maturity, bought at a discount today. Pendle's own documentation calls PT "essentially a zero-coupon bond on the underlying asset" and states that it can be redeemed 1:1 for the underlying after maturity, with the holder giving up the variable yield and any points in exchange for the fixed discount ([Pendle docs, PT](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/ProtocolMechanics/YieldTokenization/PT)).

Faq.question: Can a PT lose money if I hold to maturity?
Faq.answer: Not from rate movements, because it redeems 1:1 at maturity, but yes from the underlying asset. PT plus YT always equals the underlying, so any impairment of the yield bearing asset flows straight through to the PT ([Pendle Academy](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-academy/pendle-101/chapter-2-yield-tokenization-basics)).

Faq.question: Why did Pendle's TVL fall so far in 2026?
Faq.answer: Because yields on the assets Pendle wraps compressed. TVL fell from a September 2025 peak of $13.1 billion to roughly $1.5 billion in late April 2026, an 88 percent drawdown over seven months, alongside sUSDe APY moving from double digits to roughly 3.5 percent ([Real World Token Space](https://www.realworldtokenspace.com/research/2026-05-04-pendle-tvl-collapse-13b-to-15b-defi-fixed-income-structure-test)). Concentration made this worse: more than $4.6 billion of peak TVL, roughly 35 percent, came from Ethena yield bearing stablecoins.

Faq.question: What is Boros and how is it different from V2?
Faq.answer: Boros trades perpetual funding rates rather than spot yields. Each Yield Unit "represents the realized funding yield on 1 unit of notional, such as 1 ETH or 1 BTC, until expiry", and positions are structured as paying one interest stream and receiving another until maturity, which is the structure of an interest rate swap ([CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/08/06/pendle-lets-crypto-traders-bet-on-bitcoin-and-ether-funding-rates-with-boros-platform), [Boros Litepaper](https://docs.pendle.finance/boros-dev/LitePaper)).

Faq.question: Who governs Pendle and how do fees accrue?
Faq.answer: PENDLE holders lock into vePENDLE for up to two years, and gauge votes are snapshotted every Thursday at 00:00 UTC with a 5 percent default and 20 percent maximum pool cap ([Pendle docs, vePENDLE](https://docs.pendle.finance/ProtocolMechanics/Mechanisms/vePENDLE)). Since September 2025 the protocol routes 80 percent of holders revenue to sPENDLE, against annualised revenue of $23.97m ([DefiLlama Pendle](https://defillama.com/protocol/pendle)).

Faq.question: Is Pendle audited and is there a bug bounty?
Faq.answer: Pendle states its contracts have been audited by Ackee, Dedaub, Dingbats and top Code4rena wardens, with all reports published in the pendle-core-v2-public repository ([Pendle docs, Security](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/Security)). The Immunefi programme pays up to $250,000 for a critical smart contract finding with a $50,000 minimum and a mandatory proof of concept ([Immunefi Pendle](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/pendle/information/)).

Faq.question: Who is the counterparty if something goes wrong legally?
Faq.answer: The website and protocol are operated by Univerum Innovations Inc, an entity established under the laws of the Republic of Panama, with disputes routed to arbitration under the Singapore International Arbitration Centre ([Pendle Terms of Use](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/TermsOfUse)).

Incidents.title: Exploit
Incidents.description: Penpie, a yield booster built on Pendle, was drained for about 27 million USD through a reentrancy bug in its batchHarvestMarketRewards function. The attacker permissionlessly registered a fake Pendle market at 0x0ab305033592E16dB7D8e77d613F8d172a76ddc9 to inflate a staking balance. Penpie had been audited by WatchPug and Zokyo.
Incidents.outcome: PNP fell about 40% and PENDLE about 9%. Pendle paused all its contracts and stated its own funds were secure. LlamaRisk records that the pause safeguarded roughly 105 million USD. Exploiter address 0x7a2f4d625fb21f5e51562ce8dc2e722e12a61d1b.

Incidents.title: Depeg
Incidents.description: The guaranteed redemption price of USD0++ was changed from 1.00 USD to 0.87 USD, repricing PT-USD0++-27MAR2025 held as collateral in external lending markets. USD0++ implied APY had been capped at 30% in the oracle configuration while the asset traded above 50%.
Incidents.outcome: Documented by Chaos Labs as a case demonstrating that PT oracle configurations can be invalidated by unilateral issuer action, contributing to its recommendation against enabling PT borrowing.

Incidents.title: Oracle failure
Incidents.description: PT-ENA experienced a five minute price wick down in its oracle feed, an example of the AMM derived TWAP producing a price unrepresentative of fair value.
Incidents.outcome: Cited by Chaos Labs as evidence that PT TWAP feeds can be transiently unreliable, supporting the killswitch and safety margin design.

Incidents.title: Oracle failure
Incidents.description: For PT-weETH-27JUN2024 the Pendle team incorrectly estimated the maximum expected yield used in the market's rate configuration.
Incidents.outcome: Documented by Chaos Labs as a parameterisation error affecting PT valuation in downstream lending markets.

CATEGORY#Entity|PROTOCOL#pendle.LongDescription: Pendle splits any yield bearing token into a Principal Token (PT) and a Yield Token (YT) with a fixed maturity, so the fixed and floating legs of an onchain yield can be priced and traded separately ([Pendle docs, Introduction](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/Introduction)). A yield bearing asset is first wrapped into a Standardised Yield (SY) token, then SY is stripped into PT plus YT, and holding both is economically identical to holding the underlying ([Pendle Academy, yield tokenisation basics](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-academy/pendle-101/chapter-2-yield-tokenization-basics)). PT is described by Pendle itself as "essentially a zero-coupon bond on the underlying asset" that redeems 1:1 at maturity, while the PT holder forgoes the variable yield and points ([Pendle docs, PT](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/ProtocolMechanics/YieldTokenization/PT)). YT streams the yield until expiry and then decays to zero, which gives leveraged exposure to a yield or points stream ([Pendle docs, YT](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/ProtocolMechanics/YieldTokenization/YT)). Boros, launched in 2025, extends the same idea to perpetual funding rates, where a position "= user has to pay an interest stream and receive another interest stream until a maturity" ([Boros Litepaper](https://docs.pendle.finance/boros-dev/LitePaper)).

Risks.description: SY wrappers, PT/YT tokenization, redemption/maturity logic and the Pendle AMM are complex contracts; a bug could impair redemptions or LP funds.
Every market inherits its underlying yield source: a depeg, exploit or yield collapse of assets like Ethena sUSDe, Lido stETH or Ether.fi weETH directly hits PT/YT holders.
PT/YT valuation and liquidations on integrating protocols rely on oracles/TWAPs; stale or manipulated pricing near maturity can misvalue positions.

TVL is highly concentrated in Ethena USDe/sUSDe markets (~70%); an Ethena-specific shock would disproportionately impact Pendle. Markets are also time-bound: liquidity thins and YT decays toward maturity.
vePENDLE holders direct incentive emissions and key parameters; concentration of locked PENDLE could steer rewards or governance outcomes.
Fixed-yield and yield-trading products may face evolving regulatory treatment; Pendle is not a regulated financial product.

TypedRisks.name: Centralised admin control with no timelock
TypedRisks.description: LlamaRisk found the Pendle team retains significant central control: PendleGovernanceProxy is upgradeable immediately, admin is a 2 of 4 Safe multisig, the guardian is a single externally owned account, and there is no timelock. Admin or guardian can pause all listed contracts including PendleSY in one transaction.
TypedRisks.mitigation: PendleMarketV3 is immutable apart from pausing, so market logic cannot be rewritten. The same pause power was used constructively in September 2024.
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Any upgrade transaction on PendleGovernanceProxy, changes in multisig signer set, guardian EOA activity

TypedRisks.name: PT oracle mispricing in external lending markets
TypedRisks.description: Chaos Labs found the linear discount oracle used to price Pendle PTs as collateral can systematically underprice or overprice them, with more than 1 billion USD of PT collateral relying on it, primarily in Spark Morpho Vaults. If market price diverges downward by more than one minus the liquidation threshold, effective LTV can exceed 100% and borrowers can walk away with the debt.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Killswitch setting LTV to zero at the minimum price with a re-enable threshold of 0.9 over 3 days at 80%, safety margins recommended on the discount rate
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Spread between PT oracle price and PT AMM market price, PT collateral balances in each lending market
TypedRisks.sourceLabel: Chaos Labs ARFC on the Pendle PT risk oracle

TypedRisks.name: Bad debt and cascading liquidations from PT collateral
TypedRisks.description: Chaos Labs describes a path where oracle divergence causes rapid debt accumulation, rate agnostic utilisation spikes and cascading liquidations across markets holding PT collateral. The largest PT-sUSDe market runs a 91.5% liquidation LTV with a 25% base discount per year, leaving little margin.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Chaos Labs strongly advises against enabling PT borrowing, killswitch mechanism, conservative liquidation thresholds
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Utilisation spikes in PT collateralised markets, growth in unbacked debt positions
TypedRisks.sourceLabel: Chaos Labs ARFC on the Pendle PT risk oracle

TypedRisks.name: TWAP price floor when pool composition becomes one sided
TypedRisks.description: Pendle TWAP feeds derive only from the AMM and hit a minimum price floor when PT or SY exceeds 96% of pool composition. Beyond that point the oracle stops tracking reality.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Killswitch that sets LTV to zero when the minimum price is reached, price updates cease at 21 days to maturity for certain markets
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: PT or SY share of pool composition approaching 96%, days to maturity below 21
TypedRisks.sourceLabel: Chaos Labs ARFC on the Pendle PT risk oracle

TypedRisks.name: Underlying yield source failure passed through to PT holders
TypedRisks.description: Pendle PTs are only as good as the yield bearing asset underneath them, and LlamaRisk identified sUSDe tokenisation periods at 50.15% of TVL, WBTC at 16.79% and USD0++ at 11.02%. A failure at Ethena or Usual flows directly into the corresponding PT.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Diversification across underlying assets, LlamaRisk recommendation to delay onboarding Ethena related PTs to lending markets
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Ethena USDe collateralisation and funding rates, USD0++ redemption terms, concentration of TVL in a single underlying

TypedRisks.name: Redemption terms of an underlying can be changed unilaterally
TypedRisks.description: PT-USD0++-27MAR2025 was hit when the guaranteed redemption price of the underlying was changed from 1.00 USD to 0.87 USD, repricing the PT overnight. Nothing in Pendle prevents an issuer from changing the economics of the asset a PT is written against.
TypedRisks.mitigation: None at the Pendle layer, mitigation sits with the lending markets that accept the PT
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Issuer governance proposals affecting redemption price or floor
TypedRisks.sourceLabel: Chaos Labs ARFC on the Pendle PT risk oracle

TypedRisks.name: Implied yield assumptions set incorrectly at market creation
TypedRisks.description: Chaos Labs documents cases where yield assumptions embedded in a market were wrong: the Pendle team incorrectly estimated maximum expected yield for PT-weETH-27JUN2024, and USD0++ implied APY was capped at 30% while the asset traded above 50%.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Post hoc parameter review, external risk provider oversight
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Realised implied APY versus the cap configured for the market, maximum lnImpliedRate change per market
TypedRisks.sourceLabel: Chaos Labs ARFC on the Pendle PT risk oracle

TypedRisks.name: Permissionless market registration abused by an integrator
TypedRisks.description: The Penpie exploit worked because the attacker permissionlessly registered a fake Pendle market and used it to inflate a staking balance in Penpie's reward harvesting function. Pendle's permissionless market creation was the enabling surface even though Pendle's own contracts were not broken.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Pendle paused all contracts on discovery, safeguarding roughly 105 million USD according to LlamaRisk, and Pendle stated its own funds were secure
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: New market registrations from unknown deployers, unusual staking balance growth in integrator contracts

TypedRisks.name: Single venue liquidity and ephemeral pools
TypedRisks.description: LlamaRisk notes that PT liquidity comes from a single source, the Pendle AMM, that pools are ephemeral because they expire at maturity, and that no centralised exchange supports PTs. Exiting a large PT position before maturity depends entirely on one venue.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Deep incentivised pools for major markets, ability to hold to maturity
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: PT pool depth and slippage on a representative clip size, days to maturity

TypedRisks.name: Negative yield and principal loss on YT and PT
TypedRisks.description: LlamaRisk states that negative yield and principal loss are possible outcomes for Pendle positions. YT decays to zero at maturity and PT can trade below its expected redemption value if the underlying loses value.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Fixed maturity structure, disclosure in Pendle documentation
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Realised underlying yield versus implied yield at purchase, YT time decay curve

TypedRisks.name: Bug bounty small relative to value at risk
TypedRisks.description: LlamaRisk observed that Pendle's Immunefi bug bounty maximum of 250 thousand USD sits against roughly 5 billion USD of TVL and stated the programme could benefit from being increased. A low maximum payout weakens the incentive for whitehats to disclose rather than exploit.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Audits by ChainSecurity in August 2024 (2 medium, 9 low) and Spearbit in July 2024 (1 high, 2 medium, 5 low), plus Ackee, Dedaub, Dingbats and Code4rena wardens
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Bug bounty maximum as a percentage of TVL, audit cadence against new contract deployments

TypedRisks.name: Securities classification of Principal Tokens
TypedRisks.description: LlamaRisk records that Pendle's operating entity is domiciled in the British Virgin Islands and that the protocol relies on a 2023 opinion from a Singapore law firm that PTs are not securities. That is a single jurisdiction opinion supporting an instrument that is economically a zero coupon bond.
TypedRisks.mitigation: BVI domicile, external legal opinion, no securities enforcement action documented in the source
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: New regulatory guidance on tokenised fixed income, changes in the venues willing to list PTs

TypedRisks.name: Severe TVL contraction from the cycle peak
TypedRisks.description: Pendle TVL stood at about 935.95 million USD, against a peak of about 6.5 billion USD in June 2024 recorded by LlamaRisk. Falling TVL thins PT pool liquidity and raises exit slippage precisely when holders most want to leave.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Multi chain deployment spreading liquidity across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Plasma and others
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Total TVL trend, TVL per chain, PT pool depth per market

TypedRisks.name: Conflict of interest in third party risk assessment
TypedRisks.description: Chaos Labs disclosed in its Aave governance post that Pendle compensated Chaos Labs for the referenced risk reports. The risk parameters that gate more than 1 billion USD of PT collateral were recommended by a party paid by the issuer.
TypedRisks.mitigation: Public disclosure of the relationship in the governance thread, parallel independent review by LlamaRisk
TypedRisks.monitoringSignal: Whether risk parameter recommendations are corroborated by an unpaid reviewer
TypedRisks.sourceLabel: Chaos Labs ARFC on the Pendle PT risk oracle

CATEGORY#Entity|PROTOCOL#pendle.TradFiAnalogue: Closest instruments: the zero-coupon bond and the interest rate strip for PT and YT, and the interest rate swap for Boros.

bull.claim: PT has become accepted collateral in the largest money markets, with more than $1.6 billion of PT supplied on Aave inside a single month and the PT-sUSDe-31JUL2025 cap raised from $85m to $1.3 billion (LlamaRisk on Aave).
Boros scaled fast, exceeding $250m open interest and roughly $7 billion cumulative notional volume within about four and a half months of launch (WEEX report of BlockBeats data).

The addressable pool is enormous relative to current penetration: average open interest in the funding rate market is about $150 billion and Boros accounts for only about 0.1 percent of it (WEEX report of BlockBeats data).

Pendle settled $45 billion of value for Principal Token holders during 2025 and is pushing into KYC compliant institutional distribution, with Galaxy Curator launching on Fireblocks on 16 July 2026 (Crypto Briefing via Bitget).

bear.claim: Demand is a derivative of underlying yield. TVL fell 88 percent from $13.1 billion in September 2025 to roughly $1.5 billion by late April 2026 as sUSDe APY dropped to roughly 3.5 percent (Real World Token Space).
Single-source concentration risk is structural: more than $4.6 billion of peak TVL, roughly 35 percent, came from Ethena stablecoins (Real World Token Space).

PT liquidity is thin relative to the size of the lending exposure it backs, which is why Chaos Labs built a killswitch that sets LTV to zero when 96 percent of PT liquidity concentration thresholds are breached (Chaos Labs). Its own example, PT-eUSDe-29MAY2025 reaching $200m of deposits in 24 hours, shows how fast that exposure can build.

Revenue is modest against the size of the token economy: annualised revenue is $23.97m on $935.95m of TVL as of 26 July 2026, and the January 2026 sPENDLE upgrade was itself described as the response to revenue compression (DefiLlama Pendle, Real World Token Space).

AssetCoverage.assetStrategy: Pendle is the volume leader in yield tokenization and its asset strategy is aggressive breadth: any yield-bearing asset that can be wrapped into a Standardized Yield (SY) token can be split into a Principal Token and a Yield Token with a fixed expiry, and Pendle lists across Ethereum, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Base and Sonic. As of July 26, 2026, chain 1 alone has 58 active markets in the API. The composition of the current top book is telling: it is dominated not by liquid staking tokens but by newer synthetic dollar and RWA-flavoured assets (USDai, USDat, sUSDe, sUSDD, mAPOLLO, mHYPER, ynRWAx, superUSDC), with Lido wstETH the only large legacy LSD market and the only one running out to December 2027. The single largest market by liquidity is PT-USDai on Arbitrum at $50.4M, an order of magnitude above the next tier. What distinguishes Pendle from Spectra is the depth per market and the fact that its PT pricing has become infrastructure for other protocols: the Linear Discount Oracle is explicitly positioned as the recommended feed for money markets and has been adopted by Aave and Morpho curators including Gauntlet and Steakhouse ([Pendle oracle overview](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2-dev/Oracles/OracleOverview)).

CATEGORY#Entity|PROTOCOL#pendle.RiskPosture: Pendle's own core contracts have never been drained, and PendleMarketV3 is immutable apart from pausing, which is a real strength. The risk lives everywhere else. Governance is concentrated in a 2 of 4 multisig and a single guardian key with no timelock, which was useful in September 2024 when Pendle paused everything within a day of the Penpie exploit and protected around 105 million USD, but the same power could be turned the other way. The bigger systemic issue is that PTs became collateral across Spark, Morpho, Aave and others, priced by a discount oracle that Chaos Labs showed can drift far enough for borrowers to walk away with debt, on markets running liquidation LTVs above 91%. Add underlying concentration in sUSDe and USD0++, issuers who can change redemption terms overnight, liquidity that exists only on Pendle's own AMM, and TVL that has fallen to under 1 billion USD from a 6.5 billion USD peak, and the profile is a technically sound protocol carrying other people's risks. Treat Pendle exposure as exposure to the specific underlying and to the lending market accepting the PT, not to Pendle in the abstract.

Faq.answer: pufETH is Puffer's native liquid restaking token (nLRT). When you deposit ETH (or stETH/wstETH/WETH) you receive pufETH, which represents your stake and appreciates over time as it accrues both Ethereum proof-of-stake rewards and EigenLayer restaking rewards, while remaining liquid for use across DeFi.
Faq.question: What is pufETH?

Faq.answer: Puffer is a native liquid *restaking* protocol built on EigenLayer, so pufETH earns an additional restaking-reward layer on top of base PoS yield. It also lowers the barrier to running a validator (as little as ~1 ETH of operator bond) and uses anti-slashing hardware (Secure-Signer) rather than relying solely on operator diligence.
Faq.question: How is Puffer different from a normal liquid staking token?

Faq.answer: Secure-Signer runs validator signing inside an Intel SGX Trusted Execution Environment. Keys stay in encrypted memory and the hardware only permits signing of non-slashable messages, backed by an EIP-3076 database of past signatures. This protects against slashing from accidents, double-signing or compromised/buggy consensus clients.
Faq.question: How does Secure-Signer reduce slashing risk?

Faq.answer: PUFFER is the governance token of Puffer Protocol and the UniFi ecosystem (1 billion max supply). Holders can lock PUFFER into non-transferable vlPUFFER to gain voting power over LRT parameters, operator selection, UniFi AVS fees and UniFi Rollup upgrades, with lock multipliers up to 24x for a 24-month lock.
Faq.question: What is the PUFFER token used for?

Faq.answer: UniFi is Puffer's based-rollup roadmap. UniFi AVS is an EigenLayer service that provides preconfirmations for based rollups, and the UniFi rollup is Puffer's Layer-2 aiming to inherit Ethereum's decentralization while offering fast finality.

Faq.question: What exactly happened in the October 2024 exploit?
Faq.answer: On 16 October 2024 attackers compromised the devices of at least three Radiant developers through sophisticated malware injection. The Safe{Wallet} front-end displayed legitimate transaction data while malicious `transferOwnership` transactions were signed in the background; error messages prompted re-signing, yielding three valid malicious signatures. Tenderly simulations and manual review both returned normal, and Radiant described the compromise as completely undetectable ([Radiant post mortem](https://medium.com/@RadiantCapital/radiant-post-mortem-fecd6cd38081)). The loss is reported at roughly $50M by Radiant and crypto.news, $53M by Mandiant-linked coverage and $51M by a security researcher cited in The Block ([Crypto.news](https://crypto.news/radiant-capital-to-wind-down-after-50-million-north-korea-linked-hack/), [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/403254/unable-to-recover-from-roughly-50-million-hack-radiant-capital-is-winding-down)).

Faq.question: Who was responsible?
Faq.answer: Mandiant attributed the attack to UNC4736, also tracked as AppleJeus or Citrine Sleet, and assessed with high confidence that it has a DPRK nexus aligned with the Reconnaissance General Bureau. The initial access vector was an INLETDRIFT macOS backdoor delivered five weeks earlier via a Telegram message impersonating a former Radiant contractor ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/radiant-capital-winds-down-2m-husk-dprk-50m-heist)).

Faq.question: Why did a 3-of-11 multisig fail?
Faq.answer: Because the threshold was three and the attacker compromised three signer devices. The admin multisigs were 3-of-9 on Ethereum and Base and 3-of-11 on BSC and Arbitrum ([Radiant post mortem](https://medium.com/@RadiantCapital/radiant-post-mortem-fecd6cd38081)); The Defiant makes the point directly that the 3-of-11 configuration meant only three compromised devices were needed ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/radiant-capital-winds-down-2m-husk-dprk-50m-heist)).

Faq.question: Is Radiant still operating?
Faq.answer: No. The DAO wind-down began 1 June 2026. Lending is disabled across all Core and RIZv1 markets, RDNT emissions have ceased and treasury usage is restricted to essential matters. Users can still withdraw, repay, close positions, claim rewards and unlock dLP tokens; contracts remain immutable and accessible, the website runs until end of 2026 and the remediation portal remains available indefinitely ([Binance Square](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/329817870913330)). The Block reported the DAO's own conclusion that there was no viable path forward and that it moves to a maintenance state ([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/403254/unable-to-recover-from-roughly-50-million-hack-radiant-capital-is-winding-down)).

Faq.question: Will affected lenders be made whole?
Faq.answer: Not reliably. Eligible lending-market deposit losses are to be remediated 1:1 in kind, but only subject to available funds from protocol fees, future investments and partner contributions, and the plan explicitly does not guarantee full remediation, remaining subject to governance votes, treasury constraints and technical feasibility ([Radiant docs](https://docs.radiant.capital/radiant/remediation/remediation-plan)). Unlimited-allowance wallet drains are not eligible after a separate proposal failed quorum. With TVL at $613,179 on 26 July 2026 ([DefiLlama](https://api.llama.fi/protocol/radiant-v2)) and roughly $10.8M already laundered through Tornado Cash ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/radiant-capital-winds-down-2m-husk-dprk-50m-heist)), the recovery pool is minimal.

Faq.question: What was the roadmap before the wind-down?
Faq.answer: A February 2026 roadmap had committed to core blue-chip lending on upgraded Aave contracts plus isolated markets on Morpho, retiring the legacy RIZv1 stack. Recovery efforts included RFP-47, a merged-claim-contract approach, the Radiant Guardian Fund under RFP-52 and phased remediation for Convenience claimants, with payouts targeted for Q3 and Q4 2025 that then slipped ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/radiant-capital-winds-down-2m-husk-dprk-50m-heist), [Radiant docs](https://docs.radiant.capital/radiant/remediation/remediation-plan)).

Faq.question: Is there any residual value in RDNT?
Faq.answer: Effectively no. At the wind-down announcement RDNT traded around $0.0015 with a $1.96M market cap and a rank of #2356, and Binance, OKX and Crypto.com had all delisted it by June 2026 ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/radiant-capital-winds-down-2m-husk-dprk-50m-heist)).

CATEGORY#Entity|PROTOCOL#radiant.LongDescription: Radiant Capital was an omnichain money market: users deposited on one chain and borrowed against that collateral with withdrawals routed to other chains, initially through Stargate's stable router while collateral remained on Arbitrum ([Radiant docs](https://docs.radiant.capital/radiant/radiantv1/radiant-v1)). It was built on Aave contracts, evident in its GitHub organisation which forks `bgd-labs/aave-helpers` and `aave/aave-utilities` ([GitHub](https://github.com/radiant-capital)). The economic model paid 50% of platform fees to lenders and 50% to RDNT lockers, with RDNT rewards vesting linearly over 28 days and a 50% early-exit penalty redistributed to lockers ([Radiant docs](https://docs.radiant.capital/radiant/radiantv1/radiant-v1)). That model is now irrelevant: after the 16 October 2024 exploit the DAO began a formal wind-down on 1 June 2026, disabling lending across all Core and RIZv1 markets and ceasing RDNT emissions ([Binance Square](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/329817870913330)). What remains is a withdrawal-and-remediation shell.
